question: Consider the average difference between K-12 enrollment and 15-17 enrollment of schools that are locally funded, list the names and DOC type of schools which has a difference above this average.
evidence: Difference between K-12 enrollment and 15-17 enrollment can be computed by `Enrollment (K-12)` - `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`

SELECT 
    s.School, 
    s.DOCType
FROM 
    schools s
INNER JOIN 
    frpm f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
WHERE 
    f.`Enrollment (K-12)` - f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` > 
    (SELECT AVG(f2.`Enrollment (K-12)` - f2.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`) 
     FROM frpm f2 
     INNER JOIN schools s2 ON f2.CDSCode = s2.CDSCode 
     WHERE s2.FundingType = 'Locally Funded')
    AND s.FundingType = 'Locally Funded'

WITH SchoolEnrollmentDiff AS (
    SELECT 
        s.School,
        s.DOCType,
        f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" AS EnrollmentDiff
    FROM 
        schools s
    JOIN 
        frpm f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
    WHERE 
        s.FundingType = 'Locally Funded'
),
AvgEnrollmentDiff AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG(EnrollmentDiff) AS AvgDiff
    FROM 
        SchoolEnrollmentDiff
)
SELECT 
    sed.School,
    sed.DOCType
FROM 
    SchoolEnrollmentDiff sed
JOIN 
    AvgEnrollmentDiff aed ON sed.EnrollmentDiff > aed.AvgDiff

WITH EnrollmentDifference AS (
    SELECT
        s.School,
        s.DOCType,
        (f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") AS EnrollmentDiff
    FROM
        schools s
    INNER JOIN
        frpm f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
    WHERE
        s.FundingType = 'Locally Funded'
),
AverageDifference AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(EnrollmentDiff) AS AvgEnrollmentDiff
    FROM
        EnrollmentDifference
)
SELECT
    ed.School,
    ed.DOCType
FROM
    EnrollmentDifference ed,
    AverageDifference ad
WHERE
    ed.EnrollmentDiff > ad.AvgEnrollmentDiff

question: For all cards illustrated by Jim Pavelec. and describe the text of the ruling of these cards. Do these cards have missing or degraded properties and values.
evidence: all cards illustrated by Jim Pavelec refers to artist = 'Jim Pavelec'; the text of the ruling refers to text; cards have missing or degraded properties and values if hasContentWarning = 1 else it doesn't have;

candidates.sql:
SELECT 
    c.name,
    r.text AS ruling_text,
    CASE 
        WHEN c.hasContentWarning = 1 THEN 'Yes'
        ELSE 'No'
    END AS has_missing_or_degraded_properties
FROM 
    cards c
LEFT JOIN 
    rulings r ON c.uuid = r.uuid
WHERE 
    c.artist = 'Jim Pavelec'

Phasing out doesn’t cause any “leaves the battlefield” abilities to trigger. Similarly, phasing in won’t cause any “enters the battlefield” abilities to trigger.
Any one-shot effects that are waiting “until [this] leaves the battlefield,” such as that of Kitesail Freebooter, won’t happen when a permanent phases out.

Any continuous effects with a “for as long as” duration such as that of Awakener Druid ignore phased-out objects. Any such effects will expire if their conditions are no longer met after ignoring the phased-out objects.

question: When was the oldest mythic card released and what are its legal play formats?

    MIN(c.originalReleaseDate) AS oldest_release_date,
    l.format
FROM 
    cards c
JOIN 
    legalities l ON c.uuid = l.uuid
WHERE 
    c.rarity = 'mythic' AND l.status = 'legal'
GROUP BY 
    l.format
